section_summary.extract_value: The Discussion reports results from a single Indonesian study (Study X) validating an Indonesian version of the BAS, finding a two-factor structure where only one factor reflects body appreciation. It notes men scored higher than women on body appreciation (small effect, ηp2 = .03), no ethnic differences among Javanese, Sundanese, and Chinese participants, and a significant negative correlation between general body appreciation and BMI; limitations include opportunistic (convenience) sampling from Jakarta and lack of additional validation measures.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences used: “These results suggest that the Indonesian version of the BAS reduces to two distinct dimensions, only one of which taps the construct of body appreciation.”; “In the present study, we also found that men had significantly higher positive body appreciation than women, and the small effect size of this difference (η_p^2 = .03) is consistent with previous work.”; “In contrast, we found no significant difference in body appreciation between Javanese, Sundanese, and Chinese participants.”; “Finally, we found that general body appreciation was significantly and negatively correlated with BMI...”
